details.label: Status
details.text: first seen Nov 14 13:08. 3 jobs in 3 runs (rocm10, rocm724, scout). It passed at 01:10 on image `20261113`.

details.label: Top hypothesis
details.text: `[HIGH]` [#49603](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49603) ([`4a4f4000`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/4a4f400022105aca91bddd5d1d5af814ca59bbb1)) moved the ROCm image from UCX 1.19.x to UCX master `929abbb` (1.24.0) and a newer NIXL. After NIXL's UCX backend registers the KV cache, the next HIP stream creation fails. On rocm10 that is `hipErrorOutOfMemory` at `scheduler.py:2134`; on rocm724 it is a segfault in `hsa_queue_create`. `ucx_info` shows 1.19.1 in every passing run and 1.24.0 in the failing ones `[FACT]`.

details.label: Disconfirming
details.text: none found. The basic, PP and Mori files in the same job pass on the same image.

details.label: In-flight fix
details.text: ✅ [#50550](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/50550) (open since Nov 14 20:58) adds `UCX_ROCM_COPY_DMABUF=no` to this step. Review it; do not open a duplicate.

details.label: Suggested triage
details.text: confirm that #50550 passes on the `20261114` image, then let the author of #49603 know.

cause_prs.author: metamergebot
cause_prs.title: [Perf] [AMD] hicache: Submit staged write-back copies with hipMemcpyBatchAsync on ROCm

details.label: Status
details.text: first seen Nov 14 19:01. 3 jobs (rocm724 PR Test; scout rocm720 and rocm724). It passes on rocm10, and it passed on rocm720 on Nov 13, before the test existed.

details.label: Top hypothesis
details.text: `[MEDIUM]` [#50363](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/50363) ([`aebd76a5`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/aebd76a5f3d919bd59a8317e74dca53c7536bdfd)) added `test_hip_batch_copy_runtime_rejection`. Its `LD_PRELOAD` shim child dies with SIGSEGV on ROCm 7.2.x. Either `dlsym(RTLD_NEXT, …)` returns NULL, or the 7.2.x runtime crashes on the shim's `count=0` call.

details.label: Disconfirming
details.text: which of the two is not established. No other test in the file fails, so the production copy path is not shown to be broken.

details.label: In-flight fix
details.text: ❌ none found.

details.label: Suggested triage
details.text: run the test in the rocm724 image with `LD_DEBUG=symbols` or under gdb. Ask the PR author for a NULL check in the shim, or a ROCm 7.2.x skip.

🆕 **MiniMax-M2.7 on 8-GPU MI300 ran past the 3600 s file timeout on all three ROCm versions (scout)**: `[MEDIUM]` the cold weight load took 2651–2794 s, against about 15 s warm, and the scout's cold aiter JIT builds added to it. No change is blamed. The perf step also lost a JIT module (`ModuleNotFoundError aiter.jit.mha_batch_prefill_…`). Fix: ⚠️ [#34586](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34586) (pre-builds aiter JIT kernels, open since Aug 12) may cover the JIT part. Nothing addresses the slow storage.

🆕 **DeepSeek-V4-Flash FP8 on 8-GPU MI300, rocm724, scout only: GPU memory access fault**: `[LOW]` aiter [#7019](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7019) ([`8c964fa6`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/8c964fa61777fe5aa937da6ec8e0c8e43ce3dae1)) enabled a CK 2-stage blockscale MoE path with `swiglu_limit` that is untuned on gfx942. **Disconfirming**: one failure; an unrelated GPU fault happened on Sep 26. Fix: ❌.
🆕 **Miles compact rollout gets a `None` log-prob** (`rollout.py:147`): `[LOW]` a separate flake; it also failed on Oct 31. Fix: ❌.

details.text: re-run only if one of these recurs. Ask the runner owners about `/sgl-data` throughput on the 8-GPU MI300 pool.

fix_prs.author: kevin-mii
fix_prs.title: [Fix] [AMD] ci: Fix runner preflight and allocation cleanup

details.label: Status
details.text: 32 jobs on Nov 12, 3 on Nov 13, 35 on Nov 14 `[FACT]`:
Scout: `g26` (1-GPU) and GPU 1 of `g25` from 20:10; `g14` 21:12–22:05 (clean again at 22:12); `g13` from 22:24; `g12` at 22:27.

details.label: Top hypothesis
details.text: `[HIGH]` processes outside the runner pod hold about 300 GB on every GPU. KFD lists them, `fuser` and docker see nothing, and SIGKILL frees nothing. No change is blamed.

`[MEDIUM]` on `g13`, the 8 consecutive holder PIDs appeared 2 minutes after the crashed [`nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-deepseek-v4-flash (rocm720)`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/43636002164/job/132572857819) server on that node. That would make them a leaked server, not a stuck context.

details.label: Disconfirming
details.text: changing VRAM and non-zero CU occupancy on `g13` and `g14` point to live workloads rather than zombie contexts, and `g14` freed itself. No owner has been identified.

details.label: In-flight fix
details.text: ⚠️ [#49956](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49956) (open since Nov 12, no review) hardens the preflight only. Nothing frees the GPUs.

details.label: Suggested triage
details.text: on each node, map the KFD PIDs to pods (`/proc/<pid>/cgroup`) and take the node out of service until it is clean. Check whether a crashed job's server can outlive its pod.
